subject: bns
question: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which came into force on 1 July 2024, replaced which enactment?
explanation: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860 with effect from 1 July 2024. Section 358 of the BNS repeals the IPC while saving anything done or any action taken under it before repeal; the CrPC and the Evidence Act were replaced by the BNSS and the BSA respectively.

subject: bns
question: Murder is defined in which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
explanation: Section 101 of the BNS defines murder and its exceptions, corresponding to Section 300 of the IPC. Section 100 (old 299) defines culpable homicide, Section 103 (old 302) prescribes the punishment for murder, and Section 105 (old 304) the punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

subject: bns
question: The punishment for murder, death or imprisonment for life and fine, is prescribed by:
explanation: Section 103(1) of the BNS (old Section 302 IPC) punishes murder with death or imprisonment for life, and also with fine. Section 109 (old Section 307) deals with attempt to murder.

subject: bns
question: Causing death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that the act is likely to cause death, is defined in the BNS as:
options: culpable homicide, under Section 100 (old Section 299 IPC)
causing death by negligence, under Section 106
explanation: Section 100 of the BNS (old Section 299 IPC) defines culpable homicide in these terms. Culpable homicide is murder only if it falls within Section 101 (old Section 300) and outside its exceptions; every murder is culpable homicide, but not every culpable homicide is murder.

subject: bns
question: Theft is defined in which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
explanation: Section 303 of the BNS defines and punishes theft, corresponding to Sections 378 and 379 of the IPC. Section 308 deals with extortion, Section 309 with robbery and Section 314 with dishonest misappropriation of property.

subject: bns
question: Cheating, corresponding to Sections 415 to 420 of the IPC, is now dealt with in:
explanation: Section 318 of the BNS defines and punishes cheating, including cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property (old Section 420 IPC). Section 316 deals with criminal breach of trust, Section 336 with forgery and Section 324 with mischief.

subject: bns
question: The offence of rape, defined in Section 375 of the IPC, is now defined in:
explanation: Section 63 of the BNS defines rape (old Section 375 IPC), and Section 64 prescribes its punishment (old Section 376). Section 69 is a new provision on sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means, and Section 74 deals with assault on a woman with intent to outrage her modesty.

subject: bns
question: Where the death of a woman is caused by burns or bodily injury, or occurs otherwise than in normal circumstances, within seven years of her marriage, and she was subjected soon before her death to cruelty or harassment for dowry by her husband or his relatives, the offence is:
options: abetment of suicide, under Section 108 BNS
dowry death, under Section 80 BNS (old Section 304B IPC)
explanation: Section 80 of the BNS (old Section 304B IPC) defines dowry death in these terms and punishes it with imprisonment of not less than seven years, which may extend to imprisonment for life. The related presumption as to dowry death is in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam.

subject: bns
question: Subjecting a woman to cruelty by her husband or a relative of her husband, old Section 498A of the IPC, is now punishable under:
explanation: Section 85 of the BNS (old Section 498A IPC) punishes a husband or relative of the husband who subjects a woman to cruelty, with imprisonment up to three years and fine. Section 86 defines "cruelty" for this purpose, and Section 80 deals with dowry death.

subject: bns
question: Criminal conspiracy, defined and punished in Sections 120A and 120B of the IPC, is now dealt with in:
explanation: Section 61 of the BNS defines criminal conspiracy as an agreement between two or more persons to do an illegal act or a legal act by illegal means, and prescribes its punishment, combining old Sections 120A and 120B of the IPC. Section 45 deals with abetment and Section 62 with attempts.

subject: bns
question: When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each is liable for that act as if it were done by him alone. Under the BNS this rule (old Section 34 IPC) is in:
explanation: Section 3(5) of the BNS reproduces the rule of joint liability for acts done in furtherance of common intention (old Section 34 IPC). Section 190 (old Section 149) deals with liability of members of an unlawful assembly for offences committed in prosecution of the common object.

subject: bns
question: "Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence." This general principle (old Section 96 IPC) is in:
explanation: Section 34 of the BNS (old Section 96 IPC) states the general principle of private defence. Sections 35 to 44 (old Sections 97 to 106) set out the right of private defence of body and property, its limits, and when it extends to causing death.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 20 of the BNS (old Section 82 IPC), nothing is an offence which is done by a child under the age of:
explanation: Section 20 of the BNS (old Section 82 IPC) provides absolute immunity to a child under seven years of age. Section 21 (old Section 83) protects a child above seven and under twelve who has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature and consequences of his conduct.

subject: bns
question: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law. Under the BNS this defence is in:
explanation: Section 22 of the BNS (old Section 84 IPC) embodies the defence of unsoundness of mind, based on the M'Naghten rules. Section 23 (old Section 85) deals with acts of a person incapable of judgment by reason of involuntary intoxication.

subject: bns
question: Defamation, old Sections 499 and 500 of the IPC, is now defined and punished in Section 356 of the BNS. Which new punishment does Section 356 allow for defamation?
explanation: Section 356 of the BNS defines defamation and allows punishment of simple imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both, or community service. Community service is a new form of punishment introduced by Section 4(f) of the BNS.

subject: bns
question: Criminal breach of trust, old Sections 405 and 406 of the IPC, is now defined and punished in:
explanation: Section 316 of the BNS defines criminal breach of trust (dishonest misappropriation or conversion of property entrusted) and prescribes its punishment, combining old Sections 405 to 409 of the IPC. Section 314 deals with dishonest misappropriation and Section 317 with stolen property.

subject: bns
question: Robbery, old Sections 390 and 392 of the IPC, is now defined and punished in:
explanation: Section 309 of the BNS defines robbery (theft or extortion accompanied by causing or attempting to cause death, hurt or wrongful restraint, or fear of them) and prescribes its punishment. Section 310 (old Section 391) deals with dacoity, robbery committed by five or more persons.

subject: bns
question: Attempt to murder, old Section 307 of the IPC, is now punishable under:
explanation: Section 109 of the BNS (old Section 307 IPC) punishes attempt to murder. Section 110 (old Section 308) deals with attempt to commit culpable homicide, and Section 62 (old Section 511) is the general provision on attempts to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment.

subject: bns
question: Which new form of punishment was added to the list of punishments in Section 4 of the BNS, which had no counterpart in Section 53 of the IPC?
explanation: Section 4 of the BNS (old Section 53 IPC) lists the punishments: death, imprisonment for life, rigorous or simple imprisonment, forfeiture of property, fine and, newly, community service (Section 4(f)). Community service is prescribed for certain petty offences, such as defamation and small-value theft by first-time offenders.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 103(2) of the BNS, when a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on the ground of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other similar ground, each member of the group shall be punished with:
options: death or imprisonment for life, and fine
explanation: Section 103(2) of the BNS is a new provision on murder by a group (commonly called mob lynching): each member of a group of five or more persons who commits murder on these grounds shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and fine. The IPC had no specific provision; such cases were prosecuted under Section 302 read with Sections 34 or 149.

subject: bns
question: Organised crime, including kidnapping, robbery, extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, cyber-crimes and trafficking committed as a continuing unlawful activity by an organised crime syndicate, is a new offence under:
explanation: Section 111 of the BNS creates the new offence of organised crime, defining it and prescribing punishments ranging up to death where the offence results in death. Section 112 deals with petty organised crime and Section 113 with terrorist acts; the IPC had no equivalent general provisions.

subject: bns
question: The offence of committing a terrorist act, newly brought into the general criminal law, is in:
explanation: Section 113 of the BNS defines a terrorist act (an act done with intent to threaten the unity, integrity, sovereignty, security or economic security of India, or to strike terror in the people) and prescribes its punishment. The IPC had no such offence; terrorism was dealt with only under special laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

subject: bns
question: Suddenly or quickly or forcibly seizing, securing, grabbing or taking away from any person or his possession any movable property is the new offence of:
explanation: Section 304 of the BNS creates the new offence of snatching, a form of theft committed by suddenly, quickly or forcibly seizing or taking away movable property from a person. Under the IPC, such acts were prosecuted as theft or robbery.

subject: bns
question: Section 124A of the IPC (sedition) is not reproduced in the BNS. Which section of the BNS deals with acts endangering the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India?
explanation: Section 152 of the BNS punishes acts, by words, signs, electronic communication or financial means, that excite or attempt to excite secession, armed rebellion or subversive activities, encourage separatist feelings, or endanger the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India. It replaces the IPC's sedition offence; Section 147 (old 121) deals with waging war and Section 196 (old 153A) with promoting enmity between groups.

flags.note: Section 152 BNS replaces sedition (IPC 124A); the Supreme Court had kept 124A in abeyance in S.G. Vombatkere v. Union of India (2022). Confirm the description of Section 152.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 69 of the BNS, a man who has sexual intercourse with a woman by deceitful means, or by making a promise to marry her without any intention of fulfilling it, where such intercourse does not amount to rape, is punishable with imprisonment up to:
explanation: Section 69 of the BNS is a new provision punishing sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means (including false promises of employment or promotion, inducement, or marrying after suppressing identity) or by a false promise to marry, with imprisonment up to ten years and fine. Such cases were earlier dealt with under the IPC's rape provisions on the basis of vitiated consent.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 106(1) of the BNS, whoever causes the death of a person by a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide is punishable with imprisonment up to five years and fine. If the act is done by a registered medical practitioner while performing a medical procedure, the maximum imprisonment is:
explanation: Section 106(1) of the BNS (old Section 304A IPC) raises the maximum punishment for causing death by negligence from two to five years, but keeps it at two years for a registered medical practitioner performing a medical procedure. Section 106(2) separately deals with causing death by rash and negligent driving and escaping without reporting.

subject: bns
question: A person abets the doing of a thing who instigates any person to do that thing, engages with others in a conspiracy for doing it, or intentionally aids its doing by any act or illegal omission. This definition of abetment (old Section 107 IPC) is in:
explanation: Section 45 of the BNS (old Section 107 IPC) defines abetment of a thing in these three forms: instigation, engagement in a conspiracy, and intentional aid. Sections 46 to 60 (old Sections 108 to 120) deal with abettors and the punishment of abetment.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 62 of the BNS (old Section 511 IPC), a person who attempts to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment, where no express provision is made for its attempt, is punishable with imprisonment of any description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to:
options: one-half of the imprisonment for life or one-half of the longest term provided for the offence
the full term provided for the offence
explanation: Section 62 of the BNS (old Section 511 IPC) punishes attempts, where no express provision exists, with imprisonment up to one-half of the imprisonment for life or one-half of the longest term provided for that offence, or with the fine provided, or both. Attempt to murder and attempt to commit culpable homicide are dealt with expressly in Sections 109 and 110.

subject: bns
question: When five or more persons conjointly commit or attempt to commit a robbery, or the whole number of persons conjointly committing or attempting it, together with persons present and aiding it, amount to five or more, the offence is:
options: dacoity, under Section 310 BNS (old Section 391 IPC)
explanation: Section 310(1) of the BNS (old Section 391 IPC) defines dacoity as robbery committed or attempted conjointly by five or more persons, counting those present and aiding. The section also prescribes its punishment and the aggravated forms, such as dacoity with murder.

subject: bns
question: Intentionally putting any person in fear of any injury, and thereby dishonestly inducing the person so put in fear to deliver to any person any property, valuable security or anything signed or sealed that may be converted into a valuable security, is:
options: extortion, under Section 308 BNS (old Section 383 IPC)
explanation: Section 308 of the BNS (old Sections 383 to 389 IPC) defines extortion in these terms and prescribes its punishment. Extortion becomes robbery under Section 309 when the offender is in the presence of the person put in fear and commits it by putting that person in fear of instant death, hurt or wrongful restraint.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 137 of the BNS, kidnapping from lawful guardianship is committed by whoever takes or entices out of the keeping of the lawful guardian, without the guardian's consent:
options: a male under sixteen or a female under eighteen, as under the IPC
any person below twenty-one years of age
any child (a person below eighteen years of age) or any person of unsound mind
explanation: Section 137 of the BNS (old Sections 359 to 361 IPC) makes kidnapping from lawful guardianship gender-neutral: it covers taking or enticing any child, defined in Section 2(3) as a person below eighteen years of age, or any person of unsound mind, out of the keeping of the lawful guardian. The IPC used different ages for males (sixteen) and females (eighteen).

flags.note: Confirm that Section 137 BNS uses 'child' (below 18, gender-neutral) in place of the IPC's 16/18 ages, and the definition in Section 2(3).

subject: bns
question: Under Section 116 of the BNS (old Section 320 IPC), one of the kinds of hurt designated as grievous is any hurt which endangers life or which causes the sufferer to be in severe bodily pain, or unable to follow his ordinary pursuits, during the space of:
explanation: Section 116 of the BNS lists the kinds of grievous hurt, including emasculation, permanent privation of sight or hearing, fracture or dislocation, and any hurt endangering life or causing severe bodily pain or inability to follow ordinary pursuits for fifteen days. The IPC (Section 320, clause Eighthly) specified twenty days.

flags.note: Confirm that clause (h) of Section 116 BNS reduced the period from twenty to fifteen days.

subject: bns
question: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid, old Section 326A of the IPC, is now punishable under:
explanation: Section 124 of the BNS punishes voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid (old Section 326A IPC) with imprisonment of not less than ten years, which may extend to life, and fine to be paid to the victim. Section 124(2) punishes throwing or attempting to throw acid (old Section 326B).

subject: bns
question: A man who watches, or captures the image of, a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed commits the offence of:
options: voyeurism, under Section 77 BNS (old Section 354C IPC)
insulting the modesty of a woman, under Section 79 BNS
explanation: Section 77 of the BNS (old Section 354C IPC) defines and punishes voyeurism, including watching, capturing or disseminating the image of a woman engaging in a private act. Section 78 (old 354D) deals with stalking and Section 75 (old 354A) with sexual harassment.

subject: bns
question: A man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact, her to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest, or monitors her use of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits:
options: stalking, under Section 78 BNS (old Section 354D IPC)
explanation: Section 78 of the BNS (old Section 354D IPC) defines stalking in these terms and punishes a first conviction with imprisonment up to three years and fine, and a second or subsequent conviction with imprisonment up to five years and fine. Exceptions cover conduct pursued to prevent or detect crime or under a law.

subject: bns
question: Assaulting or using criminal force on any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that one will thereby outrage her modesty, old Section 354 of the IPC, is now punishable under:
explanation: Section 74 of the BNS (old Section 354 IPC) punishes assault or criminal force to a woman with intent to outrage her modesty, with imprisonment of not less than one year, which may extend to five years, and fine. Section 79 (old Section 509) deals with words, gestures or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 189 of the BNS (old Section 141 IPC), an assembly is designated an unlawful assembly if the common object of the persons composing it falls within the section and the assembly consists of at least:
explanation: Section 189(1) of the BNS (old Section 141 IPC) designates an assembly of five or more persons as unlawful if their common object is, for example, to overawe the Government by criminal force, resist the execution of law, or commit mischief, criminal trespass or any other offence. Section 191 (old Sections 146 and 147) deals with rioting.

subject: bns
question: If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, or such as the members knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who was a member of the assembly at the time is guilty of that offence. This rule (old Section 149 IPC) is in:
explanation: Section 190 of the BNS (old Section 149 IPC) imposes constructive liability on every member of an unlawful assembly for offences committed in prosecution of the common object. Unlike Section 3(5) (common intention), it rests on membership of the assembly and a common object rather than a prior meeting of minds.

subject: bns
question: Promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, caste or community, and doing acts prejudicial to the maintenance of harmony, old Section 153A of the IPC, is now punishable under:
explanation: Section 196 of the BNS (old Section 153A IPC) punishes promoting enmity between groups and acts prejudicial to harmony, expressly including such acts done through electronic communication. Section 197 (old 153B) deals with imputations prejudicial to national integration, and Section 299 (old 295A) with deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings.

subject: bns
question: Threatening another with any injury to his person, reputation or property, or to the person or reputation of anyone in whom he is interested, with intent to cause alarm or to cause him to do or omit any act, is:
options: criminal intimidation, under Section 351 BNS (old Sections 503 and 506 IPC)
explanation: Section 351 of the BNS defines and punishes criminal intimidation, combining old Sections 503 and 506 of the IPC. Section 352 (old Section 504) deals with intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace.

subject: bns
question: A finds a valuable ring on the road and, without knowing whose it is, immediately sells it, without taking any step to find the owner. The offence (old Section 403 IPC) is:
options: dishonest misappropriation of property, under Section 314 BNS
criminal breach of trust, under Section 316 BNS
explanation: Section 314 of the BNS (old Section 403 IPC) punishes dishonestly misappropriating or converting to one's own use any movable property. Its Explanation provides that a finder who appropriates property without using reasonable means to discover and notify the owner, and without keeping it a reasonable time for the owner to reclaim it, is guilty of this offence; it is not theft, because the property was not taken out of anyone's possession.

subject: bns
question: Dishonestly receiving or retaining any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe it to be stolen, old Section 411 of the IPC, is now punishable under:
explanation: Section 317 of the BNS defines stolen property and punishes dishonestly receiving or retaining it, combining old Sections 410 to 414 of the IPC. It also covers habitually dealing in stolen property and assisting in its concealment.

subject: bns
question: Making any false document or false electronic record, or part of one, with intent to cause damage or injury, to support a claim or title, or to commit fraud, is defined in Section 336 of the BNS (old Section 463 IPC) as:
explanation: Section 336 of the BNS defines and punishes forgery, corresponding to old Sections 463 to 465 of the IPC, including forgery for the purpose of cheating and for harming reputation. Making a false document is explained in Section 335 (old Section 464).

subject: bns
question: Causing the destruction of any property, or any change in it or its situation that destroys or diminishes its value or utility, with intent to cause, or knowing that one is likely to cause, wrongful loss or damage to the public or any person, is:
options: mischief, under Section 324 BNS (old Section 425 IPC)
explanation: Section 324 of the BNS defines and punishes mischief, combining old Sections 425 to 440 of the IPC. Its punishment is graded by the amount of loss or damage and by the means used, such as fire or explosive substances.

subject: bns
question: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets its commission is punishable under Section 108 of the BNS (old Section 306 IPC) with imprisonment up to:
explanation: Section 108 of the BNS (old Section 306 IPC) punishes abetment of suicide with imprisonment of either description up to ten years and fine. Section 107 (old Section 305) deals with abetment of suicide of a child or of a person of unsound mind, punishable with death or imprisonment for life.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 6 of the BNS (old Section 57 IPC), in calculating fractions of terms of punishment, imprisonment for life shall be reckoned as equivalent to imprisonment for:
explanation: Section 6 of the BNS (old Section 57 IPC) provides that, in calculating fractions of terms of punishment, imprisonment for life is reckoned as equivalent to imprisonment for twenty years, unless otherwise provided. It does not mean that a life sentence ordinarily ends after twenty years.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 38 of the BNS (old Section 100 IPC), the right of private defence of the body extends, subject to the restrictions in Section 37, to the voluntary causing of death of the assailant where the offence occasioning the exercise of the right is:
options: an assault with the intention of committing rape
a verbal threat to cause damage to property
explanation: Section 38 of the BNS lists the assaults against which private defence of the body extends to causing death, including assaults reasonably causing apprehension of death or grievous hurt, assault with intent to commit rape, kidnapping or abduction, and throwing or attempting to throw acid. Theft by night is relevant only to private defence of property (Section 41).

subject: bns
question: Whoever does any act with the intention of causing hurt to any person, or with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause hurt, and does cause hurt, commits voluntarily causing hurt. This offence (old Sections 321 and 323 IPC) is defined and punished in:
explanation: Section 115(1) of the BNS (old Section 321 IPC) defines voluntarily causing hurt, and Section 115(2) (old Section 323) punishes it with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to ten thousand rupees, or both. Section 114 (old Section 319) defines hurt, Section 116 (old 320) grievous hurt, and Section 117 voluntarily causing grievous hurt.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 106(2) of the BNS, whoever causes the death of a person by rash and negligent driving of a vehicle not amounting to culpable homicide, and escapes without reporting it to a police officer or a Magistrate soon after the incident, is punishable with imprisonment up to:
explanation: Section 106(2) of the BNS punishes causing death by rash and negligent driving followed by escape without reporting, with imprisonment up to ten years and fine. The IPC dealt with such deaths only under Section 304A (maximum two years), with no separate offence for escaping.

flags.note: Section 106(2) BNS (hit-and-run) was not brought into force on 1 July 2024 after transporters' protests; confirm its current status before publishing.

subject: bns
question: Section 309 of the IPC punished every attempt to commit suicide. Under the BNS:
options: attempt to commit suicide is punishable under Section 226 in all cases
there is no general offence of attempting suicide; Section 226 punishes only an attempt to commit suicide with intent to compel or restrain any public servant from discharging official duty
attempt to commit suicide is punishable with community service under Section 4
attempt to commit suicide is punishable as attempt to murder under Section 109
explanation: The BNS does not reproduce Section 309 of the IPC as a general offence. Section 226 of the BNS punishes attempting to commit suicide with intent to compel or restrain any public servant from discharging his official duty, with simple imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both, or community service.

flags.note: Confirm the section number (226) and punishment for attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain exercise of lawful power.

subject: bns
question: Adultery, which was an offence under Section 497 of the IPC, is under the BNS:
options: not an offence, the BNS not having reproduced Section 497, which the Supreme Court had struck down
punishable only on the complaint of the husband
explanation: The Supreme Court struck down Section 497 of the IPC as unconstitutional in Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018), and the BNS does not reproduce it, so adultery is not an offence. Adultery may still be a ground for divorce under personal laws.

flags.note: Based on Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018). Confirm the statement that Section 84 BNS is not an adultery provision (it deals with enticing or detaining a married woman).

subject: bns
question: Under Section 21 of the BNS (old Section 83 IPC), nothing is an offence which is done by a child above seven years of age and under twelve years who:
options: is in the custody of a guardian
has not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature and consequences of his conduct on that occasion
acted under the instigation of an adult
has not been sent to school
explanation: Section 21 of the BNS (old Section 83 IPC) gives a qualified immunity to a child above seven and under twelve, depending on proof that he had not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature and consequences of his conduct on that occasion. A child under seven enjoys absolute immunity under Section 20.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 23 of the BNS (old Section 85 IPC), a person who, at the time of doing an act, is incapable of knowing its nature or that it is wrong or contrary to law, by reason of intoxication, is protected only if:
options: the intoxication was caused by alcohol
the thing which intoxicated him was administered to him without his knowledge or against his will
he was intoxicated for the first time
he voluntarily drank in a licensed place
explanation: Section 23 of the BNS (old Section 85 IPC) protects a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication only where the intoxicant was administered to him without his knowledge or against his will. Under Section 24 (old Section 86), a person who voluntarily becomes intoxicated is treated as having the same knowledge as if he were not intoxicated.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 28 of the BNS (old Section 90 IPC), a consent is NOT such a consent as is intended by any section of the Sanhita if it is given:
options: by a person under fear of injury or under a misconception of fact, and the person doing the act knows or has reason to believe this
by a person above eighteen years of age
explanation: Section 28 of the BNS (old Section 90 IPC) provides that consent given under fear of injury or under a misconception of fact, where the doer knows or has reason to believe it, is not valid consent. It also excludes consent given by a person of unsound mind or intoxicated who cannot understand its nature, and, unless the context otherwise requires, consent given by a person under twelve years of age.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 41 of the BNS (old Section 103 IPC), the right of private defence of property extends to the voluntary causing of death where the offence occasioning the exercise of the right is, among others:
options: simple theft by day without any threat
robbery, house-breaking after sunset and before sunrise, or mischief by fire or explosive substance on a building used as a human dwelling
explanation: Section 41 of the BNS (old Section 103 IPC) extends private defence of property to causing death in cases of robbery, house-breaking after sunset and before sunrise, mischief by fire or explosive substance on a building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling or for custody of property, and theft, mischief or house-trespass causing reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 104 of the BNS (old Section 303 IPC), whoever, being under sentence of imprisonment for life, commits murder, shall be punished with:
options: death only, as a mandatory sentence
death, or imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person's natural life
explanation: Section 104 of the BNS punishes murder by a life-convict with death or with imprisonment for life meaning the remainder of the person's natural life. Section 303 of the IPC had prescribed a mandatory death sentence, which the Supreme Court struck down in Mithu v. State of Punjab (1983).

flags.note: Mentions Mithu v. State of Punjab (1983). Confirm the wording of the punishment in Section 104 BNS.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 70(2) of the BNS, where a woman under eighteen years of age is raped by one or more persons constituting a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention, each of them shall be punished with:
options: imprisonment of not less than ten years
imprisonment for life, which shall mean the remainder of that person's natural life, and fine, or with death
explanation: Section 70(2) of the BNS punishes gang rape of a woman under eighteen with imprisonment for life for the remainder of natural life and fine, or with death. The IPC had separate provisions for gang rape of women under twelve and under sixteen (Sections 376DA and 376DB); the BNS consolidates them under the age of eighteen.

flags.note: Confirm the age threshold (under 18) and punishment in Section 70(2) BNS against the bare act.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 303(2) of the BNS, on the first conviction of a person for theft where the value of the stolen property is less than five thousand rupees and the property has been returned or restored, the person shall be punished with:
options: fine of not less than ten thousand rupees
explanation: The proviso to Section 303(2) of the BNS provides that on the first conviction of a person for theft, where the value of the property is less than five thousand rupees and it has been returned or restored, the punishment shall be community service. The general punishment for theft is imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both (old Section 379 IPC).

flags.note: Confirm the Rs. 5,000 limit and the community-service proviso to Section 303(2) BNS.

subject: bns
question: Under Section 111 of the BNS, "continuing unlawful activity" by an organised crime syndicate means an activity prohibited by law, a cognizable offence punishable with imprisonment of three years or more, in respect of which:
options: at least one FIR has been registered in the preceding year
more than one charge-sheet has been filed before a competent court within the preceding ten years and that court has taken cognizance
a conviction has been recorded within the preceding five years
the National Investigation Agency has registered a case
explanation: Section 111 of the BNS defines continuing unlawful activity as a cognizable offence punishable with three years or more, undertaken by a person as a member of or on behalf of a syndicate, in respect of which more than one charge-sheet has been filed within the preceding ten years and the court has taken cognizance. The definition follows the pattern of State organised-crime laws such as MCOCA.

subject: bns
question: Section 95 of the BNS, which has no counterpart in the IPC, punishes whoever:
options: hires, employs or engages any child to commit an offence
sells a child for the purpose of begging
fails to send a child to school
explanation: Section 95 of the BNS creates a new offence of hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence, with imprisonment of not less than three years, which may extend to ten years, and fine. If the offence is committed by the child, the person hiring him is punished as if he had committed it himself.
